newsitem.title: THAILAND: Cambodians flee war only to land in Thai jails.
newsitem.headline: Cambodians flee war only to land in Thai jails.

text.p: For some Cambodians, freedom was fleeting.

A group of 41 Cambodian citizens managed to scramble aboard Thai evacuation flights to flee fighting in their homeland on Tuesday. Like the hundreds of Thais and other foreigners on the flights they rejoiced as soon as they touched Thai soil.
But they had only a few minutes to enjoy the feeling of safety before they were put in jail by Thai immigration police.

"They rushed to take a free ride in the Thai evacuation plane and ended up with a free night in a Thai cell," Sar Sambath, Minister Consellor at the Cambodian embassy in Bangkok, told Reuters on Wednesday.
"The Thai embassy in Phnom Penh issued the documents for them to board the Thai evacuation plane to Bangkok and I don't understand why they were charged for illegal entry," Sar Sambaht said.
The consellor said he spent the entire day bailing out the evacuees from the immigration detention centre and put them all in a cheap hotel where they waited to be sent back home.

The Thai Air Force sent eight C-130 planes and evacuated more than 700 Thais and nearly 100 foreigners from Phnom Penh on Tuesday after the capital was hit by two days of fighting and a day of widespread looting and violence as forces loyal to the rival premiers battled for power.
